cues.zh: 和其他一些分会场正在进行的也有点不同，但我们希望

cues.zh: 这场会议能让你们稍微了解一下

cues.zh: 我们在Facebook自己内部是怎么做的

cues.en: to build our own apps and to launch them to the world.

cues.zh: 我很喜欢Facebook工程团队的一点就是

cues.en: How we like to move fast and break things or
cues.zh: 我们如何喜欢快速行动、打破常规，或者

cues.zh: 交付稳定的基础设施，

cues.en: and
cues.zh: 以及

cues.en: how we ship love to our users around the world.
cues.zh: 我们如何向全世界的用户传递爱。

cues.en: We also like to tell stories
cues.zh: 我们也喜欢讲故事

cues.en: about the challenges that we constantly face as an organization, as a company.
cues.zh: 关于我们作为一个组织、一家公司不断面临的挑战。

cues.en: We like to talk about those challenges brought on by moving
cues.zh: 我们喜欢聊那些因为我们的行动速度

cues.en: at the speed we move
cues.zh: 和业务规模

cues.en: and at the scale of our business.
cues.zh: 而带来的挑战。

cues.en: But more importantly, we like to talk about the solutions that we've come up with to those challenges.
cues.zh: 但更重要的是，我们喜欢聊我们针对这些挑战想出的解决方案。

cues.en: Whether they be innovative ideas,
cues.zh: 无论是创新的想法、

cues.en: software libraries,
cues.zh: 软件库、

cues.en: tools,
cues.zh: 工具、

cues.en: processes,
cues.zh: 流程，

cues.en: and we like to talk about how we then go on and share those with the world through our open source program
cues.zh: 我们还喜欢聊我们如何通过开源项目把这些分享给全世界

cues.en: and through forums like this one.
cues.zh: 以及通过像这样的论坛。

cues.en: So I'm thrilled to introduce the session this afternoon. The track is gonna take us on a journey. It's gonna talk about many, many aspects of our engineering business. We're gonna start off talking about some of our web infrastructure,
cues.zh: 所以我很激动来介绍今天下午的这场会议。这个专场将带我们踏上一段旅程。它会谈到我们工程业务的许多许多方面。我们会先从一些Web基础设施谈起，

cues.en: on the front and on the back end.
cues.zh: 包括前端和后端。

cues.en: Then we're gonna spin across the mobile and you're gonna hear from the team that built our messenger app.
cues.zh: 接下来我们将转向移动端，大家会听到我们 Messenger 团队的分享。

cues.en: One of our primary standalone Facebook apps. You're gonna hear from the paper team about how they built their new iOS app. We're gonna hear from the Android team who are shipping high quality products
cues.zh: 这是我们主要的独立 Facebook 应用之一。大家会听到 Paper 团队讲述他们如何构建全新的 iOS 应用。我们还会听到 Android 团队的分享，他们正将高质量的产品

cues.en: to hundreds of thousands, hundreds of millions of users.
cues.zh: 带给成千上万、数以亿计的用户。

cues.zh: 你还会听到发布团队的分享，他们的职责是将所有这些产品推送到应用商店，并交到广大用户手中。

cues.zh: 我叫 James，但我今天只有一个任务，

cues.en: and that is to get off the stage as quickly as possible,
cues.zh: 那就是尽快下台，

cues.en: and make room for the teams that are gonna take you on this journey.
cues.zh: 给即将带大家开启这段旅程的团队腾出时间。

cues.en: So without further ado, I'd like to introduce from our
cues.zh: 闲话少说，我想隆重介绍来自我们

cues.en: front end web infrastructure team,
cues.zh: 前端 Web 基础设施团队的

cues.en: Jing,
cues.zh: Jing、

cues.en: Pete, and to kick us all off, Tom.
cues.zh: Pete，以及为我们打头阵的 Tom。

cues.en: Awesome.
cues.zh: 太棒了。

cues.zh: James，非常感谢你的介绍。坐在那边软沙发上的各位能听到我说话吗？

cues.en: All good? It's worth noting, all this seating, this actually came from our office. We shipped it all in so that we could, you know, make this space as comfortable as possible. I think we have the best room in the house here. Certainly the most comfortable in my opinion.
cues.zh: 都听得到吧？顺便说一下，这些沙发其实都是从我们办公室搬来的。我们把它们全运过来，就是为了，你知道的，让这个场地尽可能舒服。我觉得我们占了全场最好的房间。至少在我看来是最舒服的。

cues.en: So welcome.
cues.zh: 欢迎大家。

cues.en: I'm Tom O'Kino
cues.zh: 我是 Tom O'Kino，

cues.en: and I manage the JavaScript infrastructure team at Facebook.
cues.zh: 我在 Facebook 管理 JavaScript 基础设施团队。

cues.en: One more?
cues.zh: 还有吗？

cues.en: So I work on a bunch of stuff. I've worked on a bunch of stuff over the years. I still write code whenever I can even as a manager.
cues.zh: 我做过很多项目。这些年来我参与过各种项目。即使身为管理者，只要有机会我还是会写代码。

cues.en: And over the years I've built a lot different things. I've worked on a lot of different projects.
cues.zh: 多年来我构建过很多不同的东西，参与过许多不同的项目。

cues.en: But one of the things that I've tried to do over the years, the thing that holds everything together, the thing that, you know, kind of ties everything that I've worked on together is I was always trying to build quality software.
cues.zh: 但这么多年来我一直尝试做的一件事、贯穿一切的核心、也就是把我的所有工作串联起来的东西，其实就是我一直在努力构建高质量的软件。

cues.en: This is what we're all trying to do. Right? We're trying to do this at Facebook. All of you, if you have startups or you work at companies, you're trying to build high quality software.
cues.zh: 这也是我们所有人都在努力做的事，对吧？我们在 Facebook 也在努力做到这一点。你们大家，无论是在创业公司还是在各大企业工作，也都在努力构建高质量的软件。

cues.en: So let's talk for a minute about what quality software actually means. Right? There's a few important pieces here.
cues.zh: 所以我们花一分钟聊聊，高质量软件到底意味着什么，好吗？这里有几个关键的组成部分。

cues.en: The most important piece is whatever you're building, if it's an app or a feature or a product or whatever it is, it needs to add value. It needs to really add value to someone's life.
cues.zh: 其中最重要的一点是，无论你在构建什么，是一个应用、一个功能、一款产品还是别的什么，它都需要创造价值。它必须切切实实地为某人的生活增添价值。

cues.en: It needs to be useful and provide utility.
cues.zh: 它需要有用，并且能够提供实际的效用。

cues.en: If you don't provide utility and you don't value to someone's life, then the rest of this doesn't matter. We don't even need to talk about it.
cues.zh: 如果你提供不了效用，也无法为别人的生活带来价值，那么其余的一切都毫无意义，我们甚至都不用讨论了。

cues.en: But once you have a good idea
cues.zh: 但一旦你有了一个好点子

cues.en: and you produce something
cues.zh: 并且你生产出了某些东西

cues.en: that adds value to someone's life, there's a couple other things we need to focus on.
cues.zh: 能够为别人的生活增添价值，那么我们还需要关注另外几件事。

cues.en: For our software to be quality, we need it to be reliable.
cues.zh: 为了让我们的软件达到高质量，我们需要它具备可靠性。

cues.en: We need it to be high performance. The user experience has to be great.
cues.zh: 我们需要它具有高性能，用户体验必须极佳。

cues.en: We also need it to be enjoyable and easy to use.
cues.zh: 我们还需要它令人愉悦且易于使用。

cues.en: Does it make sense to everybody? Kind of agree? Has to be good?
cues.zh: 大家觉得有道理吗？差不多都同意？必须得做好？

cues.en: The thing is is that quality takes time
cues.zh: 问题在于，高质量是需要时间的

cues.en: and in fact, the higher quality you want your application or your product to be,
cues.zh: 事实上，你希望你的应用或产品质量越高，

cues.en: the more time you kind of have to put into it.
cues.zh: 你往往就得投入越多的时间。

cues.en: Does that resonate with anyone?
cues.zh: 有人有同感吗？

cues.en: But one of Facebook's core values and one of the things that we value the most is our ability to move fast. This is really important to us.
cues.zh: 但 Facebook 的核心价值观之一、也是我们最看重的能力之一，就是快速行动。这对我们非常重要。

cues.en: We need to be able to go from an idea that an engineer or somebody has
cues.zh: 我们需要能够把工程师或其他人的一个想法，

cues.en: to in production, in people's hands as quickly as we possibly can.
cues.zh: 以最快的速度推向生产环境，送到用户手中。

cues.en: And then once it's in production, we need to collect feedback and metrics and data and we need to iterate on that thing as fast as we possibly can.
cues.zh: 一旦上线生产，我们就需要收集反馈、指标和数据，并以最快的速度对产品进行迭代。

cues.en: So that we can get to the best possible product.
cues.zh: 这样我们才能打造出最好的产品。

cues.en: Now it seems these two things are at odds with each other. On the one hand, we want to produce something that's really high quality and we know that's going to take some time. But on the other hand, we know that we need to be able to move fast and get to market as quickly as we possibly can
cues.zh: 现在看来，这两者似乎是矛盾的。一方面，我们想做出高质量的东西，而我们知道这需要时间。但另一方面，我们知道我们需要快速行动，尽快推向市场，

cues.en: or else somebody will do it before us.
cues.zh: 否则别人就会抢先一步。

cues.en: Is there a way that we can produce higher quality software
cues.zh: 有没有什么办法，能让我们在更短的时间内，

cues.en: in less time?
cues.zh: 开发出更高质量的软件呢？

cues.en: Well, we could try a bunch of different things. We can try cutting features from whatever we were building. Right? We can try saying, oh, you know what? This feature, we don't have time to build it. We need the rest of this experience to be high quality. We're just gonna cut it.
cues.zh: 其实，我们可以尝试很多不同的方法。比如我们可以砍掉正在开发的功能。对吧？我们可以说：“噢，你知道吗？这个功能我们没时间做了。为了保证其余体验的高质量，我们直接把它砍掉。”

cues.en: Well, listen. A minute ago, were talking about adding value.
cues.zh: 听着，一分钟前我们聊到了增加价值。

cues.en: If we were trying to build a minimum viable product, cutting features isn't an option. You no longer are adding the value that you seek... That you were trying to seek out to aim
cues.zh: 如果我们想打造最小可行产品，削减功能并不是选项。你就不再增加你所追求的价值……你原本试图寻找并瞄准的价值

cues.en: to build.
cues.zh: 去构建。

cues.en: So what about adding engineers? Can we just add as many engineers to this as possible? Get it done super quick?
cues.zh: 那么增加工程师呢？我们能不能尽可能多地加工程师？快速搞定？

cues.en: Well, anybody who knows anything about the mythical man month knows that you can't just throw more engineers at this problem.
cues.zh: 任何了解《人月神话》的人都知道，你不能只是往这个问题上扔更多工程师。

cues.en: You can't just add people to the project and expect that it's gonna get done really quickly and super high quality.
cues.zh: 你不能只是往项目里加人，就指望它很快完成而且质量超高。

cues.en: What about just asking all of our existing engineers to work harder? Alright, everybody, for the next three months we're going to work for eighty hours a week. Cool?
cues.zh: 那让所有现有工程师更努力地工作呢？好，各位，接下来三个月我们每周工作八十小时。行吗？

cues.en: Right? That's obviously not sustainable.
cues.zh: 对吧？这显然不可持续。

cues.en: What we really want to do here is we want to change the math on this.
cues.zh: 我们真正想在这里做的是改变这个算式。

cues.en: We want to make it so that we produce higher code,
cues.zh: 我们想做到的是产出更高的代码，

cues.en: higher quality software
cues.zh: 更高质量的软件

cues.en: and better code by default.
cues.zh: 默认写出更好的代码。

cues.en: And we want to do it in less time.
cues.zh: 而且我们要用更少的时间做到。

cues.en: So we've experimented with a bunch of different ways to do this especially on web. I'll talk about one of those things.
cues.zh: 所以我们尝试了很多不同的方法，尤其是在 Web 上。我来聊其中一件事。

cues.en: We tried MVC. We tried this a lot of places on the web and what we found is that in our sufficiently large code base, in our sufficiently large organization,
cues.zh: 我们试过 MVC。我们在 Web 上很多地方试过，结果发现，在我们足够大的代码库中，在我们足够大的组织里，

cues.en: MVC got really complicated
cues.zh: MVC 变得非常复杂

cues.en: really really quickly.
cues.zh: 非常非常快就变复杂了。

cues.en: Now Jing is going to talk more about this in a few minutes but I want to describe what actually happened.
cues.zh: 接下来几分钟 Jing 会详细讲这个，但我想先说明事情究竟是怎么发生的。

cues.en: Every time that we tried to add a new feature to one of these systems, the complexity of the entire system
cues.zh: 每次我们尝试给其中一个系统添加新功能时，整个系统的复杂度

cues.en: just blew up. Right? It wasn't just the new feature that added a little bit of weight to our code base but everything kind of got more complicated.
cues.zh: 都会一下子膨胀起来。对吧？增加的并不只是新功能给代码库带来的一点负担，而是所有东西都变得更复杂了。

cues.en: What was going on is the code was responsible for doing more things and the data was used in more places so our code got really unpredictable.
cues.zh: 问题在于，代码负责做更多事情，数据也被更多地方使用，所以我们的代码变得非常难以预测。

cues.en: And what I mean by unpredictable
cues.zh: 我所说的难以预测

cues.en: is that a new engineer coming into our code base,
cues.zh: 是指新加入的工程师

cues.en: looking at code for the first time
cues.zh: 第一次查看我们的代码时

cues.en: would have a hard time getting up to speed. They'd have some task that they're trying to complete and it would take them a long time to kind of actually be able to be productive in that code base because they didn't necessarily trust what was going on. They couldn't make changes to that code easily
cues.zh: 会很难快速上手。他们可能有一项任务要完成，但要花很长时间才能真正开始在这个代码库中高效工作，因为他们不一定能信任代码的行为。他们没法轻易修改这部分代码

cues.en: because they were afraid of what was gonna happen.
cues.zh: 因为他们担心会引发什么问题。

cues.en: So, you know, they have the one engineer who actually built this thing and they go to that person and they say, hey, you know, I need to make some changes here.
cues.zh: 所以，他们只能去找那个真正构建了这套东西的工程师，说：“嘿，我需要在这里做一些修改。”

cues.en: Right? If you have one engineer who is the only person willing to touch an area of your code base, that code might be a little bit unpredictable. Has anybody ever experienced that?
cues.zh: 对吧？如果你的代码库中有一块区域，只有一个工程师愿意碰它，那这部分代码可能就有点难以预测。有人遇到过这种情况吗？

cues.en: You know, like one person? Yeah. Right? There's only one person that'll that'll make that change.
cues.zh: 你知道，就像一个人？对。对吧？只有一个人会做出那个改变。

cues.en: So this became really hard for us. You know, we were moving really slow because our code was fragile and unpredictable.
cues.zh: 所以这对我们来说变得非常困难。你知道，我们推进得很慢，因为代码脆弱又不可预测。

cues.en: So for us at least, know, MVC kind of fell apart.
cues.zh: 所以至少对我们来说，你知道，MVC 有点崩了。

cues.en: What we thought is that if we can increase the predictability of our code base, we can make it so that new engineer coming in can get up to speed really quickly and make changes more confidently.
cues.zh: 我们的想法是，如果能提高代码库的可预测性，就能让新来的工程师很快上手，更有信心地做修改。

cues.en: We
cues.zh: 我们

cues.en: thought we'd be able to produce higher quality applications
cues.zh: 本以为我们能产出更高质量的应用程序

cues.en: in less time by just making our code, just structuring our code a little bit differently
cues.zh: 用更少的时间，只要把代码、把代码结构稍微调整一下

cues.en: in a way that makes it more predictable.
cues.zh: 让它更具可预测性。

cues.en: Okay? So this is what we're going be talking about today.
cues.zh: 好吗？这就是我们今天要讲的内容。

cues.en: We're going to be talking about two systems, an architecture and then framework.
cues.zh: 我们要讲两个系统：一个架构，然后是一个框架。

cues.en: Flux is a system architecture that encourages
cues.zh: Flux 是一种系统架构，它鼓励

cues.en: single directional data flow through your application
cues.zh: 应用中的单向数据流

cues.en: and Jing is going to come up and talk about that in a minute.
cues.zh: 而 Jing 一会儿会上来讲这个。

cues.en: React is a is a framework
cues.zh: React 是一个框架

cues.en: that allows you to build user interfaces in a way that is a lot more predictable, a lot more declarative
cues.zh: 它让你能以更可预测、更具声明式的方式构建用户界面

cues.en: and we think a lot more powerful.
cues.zh: 而且我们认为它强大得多。

cues.en: And at least anecdotally speaking, React has allowed us to move a lot faster internally at Facebook and now we're seeing that same success
cues.zh: 至少从实际经验看，React 让我们在 Facebook 内部推进得快多了，现在我们看到同样的成功

cues.en: throughout the internet since we open sourced this last year and released it, you know, back in in May of last year.
cues.zh: 在整个互联网上，自从我们去年开源并发布它，你知道，去年五月。

cues.en: So with that, I'm gonna invite Jing up to tell us a little bit about the first system for managing our our data called Flux.
cues.zh: 那么接下来，我有请 Jing 上台来为我们讲讲管理我们数据的第一个系统——Flux。

cues.en: Great.
cues.zh: 太棒了。

cues.en: Alright. Thanks, Tom. So my name is Jing
cues.zh: 好的。谢谢 Tom。我叫 Jing，

cues.en: and I'm a software engineer on the product infrastructure team at Facebook.
cues.zh: 是 Facebook 产品基础设施团队的一名软件工程师。

cues.en: So let's talk about some of the problems behind MVC
cues.zh: 那我们来聊聊 MVC 背后的某些问题，

cues.en: that make it not scale,
cues.zh: 正是这些问题导致它无法扩展，

cues.en: and how Flex proposes to solve some of those problems.
cues.zh: 以及 Flex 是如何提出解决方案来解决其中一些问题的。

cues.en: Well, MVC works pretty well for small applications.
cues.zh: 嗯，MVC 对于小型应用来说运行得相当不错。

cues.en: Everything has its own particular role to play.
cues.zh: 每个部分都有其特定的角色。

cues.en: The problem is that it doesn't make room for new features.
cues.zh: 问题在于它没有为新功能留出空间。

cues.en: Let's look at what happens to this diagram when we add a lot of models and when we add a lot of views to the system.
cues.zh: 让我们看看当我们在系统中添加大量模型和视图时，这个图表会变成什么样。

cues.en: There's just an explosion of arrows.
cues.zh: 箭头直接呈指数级爆炸增长。

cues.en: And if you just look at these arrows, can you tell if there's an infinite loop here where the model triggers something in the view and the view triggers something in a different model? It goes in a cycle.
cues.zh: 如果只看这些箭头，你能看出这里是否存在死循环吗？比如模型触发了视图中的某些东西，而视图又触发了另一个模型中的东西？它形成了一个循环。

cues.en: It's really hard to tell just by looking at this, and that's with all of your relationships drawn out. If you were to look at that in code and try to figure out, where do I have an infinite loop somewhere in here that's causing my app to just go in constant loops? It's really difficult.
cues.zh: 光看这个真的很难分辨，而且这还是在你把所有关系都画出来的情况下。如果你在代码中看这个，试图找出：我的应用到底哪里有个死循环，导致它一直在不断地循环？这真的很难。

cues.en: I was drawing a very similar diagram while I was trying to figure out the architecture of one of our more complicated interfaces.
cues.zh: 当我试图弄清楚我们一个较复杂的界面的架构时，我也画过一张非常类似的图。

cues.en: It looked very much like this, and it was so complicated that I ended up drawing numbers instead of arrows to represent the relationships between them. That's how dense the arrows were getting.
cues.zh: 它看起来大致是这样，而且复杂到我最后用数字而不是箭头来表示它们之间的关系。箭头密集到了这种程度。

cues.en: So we want to do away with all of this. What we proposed instead is something called flux. It's a single directional data flow.
cues.zh: 所以我们想摆脱这一切。我们提出的方案叫做 flux。它是单向数据流。

cues.en: And that avoids all of the double arrows that go in both directions that make it really hard to understand the system.
cues.zh: 这样就避免了所有双向的箭头，那些箭头让系统很难理解。

cues.en: What we have is an action coming into the system, a dispatcher that sort of acts as the traffic controller for the whole thing,
cues.zh: 我们的做法是：一个 action 进入系统，一个 dispatcher 充当整个系统的交通指挥，

cues.en: the store, which is the data layer that basically updates whenever you get a new action, and then the views rerender whenever the stores say something has changed.
cues.zh: 然后是 store，它是数据层，基本上每当收到新的 action 就更新，之后只要 store 说有什么变了，视图就会重新渲染。

cues.en: And then from the view side,
cues.zh: 然后从视图这一侧，

cues.en: they can throw another action back into the system.
cues.zh: 它们可以把另一个 action 抛回系统。

cues.en: The dispatcher here is the main
cues.zh: 这里的 dispatcher 是主要的

cues.en: piece that enforces that there's no cascading effects.
cues.zh: 部件，它确保不会出现级联效应。

cues.en: Once an action goes into the store, you can't put another one in until
cues.zh: 一旦一个 action 进入 store，你就不能再放入另一个，直到

cues.en: the stores are completely finished processing it. That's pretty abstract though, so let's work our way back to this, and let's use a real world example, a chat interface at Facebook.
cues.zh: store 完全处理完它。不过这太抽象了，所以我们回到这张图，用一个真实世界的例子：Facebook 的聊天界面。

cues.en: We knew that we had a problem with chat in 2011
cues.zh: 我们知道 2011 年聊天功能有问题

cues.en: when we introduced
cues.zh: 当时我们推出了

cues.en: the subscribe button on our blog,
cues.zh: 博客上的订阅按钮，

cues.en: and the first comment on that blog post was, please improve chat system with eight ninety eight likes.
cues.zh: 而那篇博文的第一条评论是：请改进聊天系统，898 个赞。

cues.en: And this was one of our more polite requests.
cues.zh: 这也是我们收到比较客气的诉求之一。

cues.en: We got a lot of comments that would just say, fix chat, and that became a pretty frequent refrain in all of our user comments.
cues.zh: 我们收到了很多评论，直言“修一下聊天功能”，这几乎成了我们用户评论中经常出现的旋律。

cues.en: So how do we get to this place? How do we get to the point where we were annoying our users so much, they just wanted us to fix chat? They didn't care what else we were launching. They didn't care we were improving. They just wanted us to fix chat.
cues.zh: 那么，我们是怎么走到这一步的呢？我们是怎么惹得用户如此烦恼，以至于只想让我们修好聊天功能？他们根本不在乎我们还发布了什么，不在乎我们做了什么改进，他们只想让我们修好聊天功能。

cues.en: Well, to answer that, we have to go through sort of
cues.zh: 嗯，为了回答这个问题，我们得回顾一下

cues.en: the chat feature as it evolved.
cues.zh: 聊天功能的演变过程。

cues.en: We started with something pretty simple. You have a chat tab. It shows a list of messages.
cues.zh: 我们最初的功能非常简单。你有一个聊天标签页，它会显示消息列表。

cues.en: Whenever you want to... Whenever you get a new chat message, you just append it. It's pretty simple.
cues.zh: 每当你……每当收到一条新的聊天消息，你只需把它追加到后面。非常简单。

cues.en: The code is pretty manageable.
cues.zh: 代码也相当好维护。

cues.en: Later on, we also launched the messages jewel, which shows you the number of threads that have unseen messages on them.
cues.zh: 后来，我们还推出了消息红点提示（messages jewel），用来显示有未读消息的线程数量。

cues.en: That was kind of developed independently from the chat tab.
cues.zh: 这个功能开发时跟聊天标签页基本上是独立的。

cues.en: But whenever a a new message comes in, we also want to handle that unseen count. So this code gets a little bit more complicated. We have an unseen
cues.zh: 但每当有新消息进来时，我们还需要处理这个未读计数。于是这段代码变得稍微复杂了一点。每收到一条新消息，我们都要让未读

cues.en: thread count that we want to bump every time we get a new message. And if we think that the user is looking at it, we also want to decrement it.
cues.zh: 线程数加一；而如果我们认为用户正在查看它，我们还要把它减一。

cues.en: A couple months later, we also introduced the larger messages view.
cues.zh: 几个月后，我们又推出了更大尺寸的消息视图。

cues.en: And with that, we made this handler even more complicated.
cues.zh: 随之而来的是，我们把这个处理逻辑搞得更加复杂了。

cues.en: This is what we had before.
cues.zh: 这就是我们以前的做法。

cues.en: And now we have to sort of account for the messages view and decrement the count under the right conditions, if we think the user is looking at either one of the views.
cues.zh: 现在，如果觉得用户正在查看其中某个视图，我们就得处理消息视图，并在正确条件下递减计数。

cues.en: So what are the problems here?
cues.zh: 那么这里有什么问题呢？

cues.en: One is that the code really
cues.zh: 首先是这段代码

cues.en: has no structure.
cues.zh: 完全没有结构。

cues.en: It's very imperative. That makes it fragile.
cues.zh: 它是高度命令式的，这让它变得很脆弱。

cues.en: And we lose a lot of the original intents behind it. It's hard to tell just by looking at the code that you want to keep the messages view and the chat tab view in sync. It's hard to tell that you only want to increment and then decrement.
cues.zh: 而且我们丢失了许多背后的原始意图。光看代码很难看出你想让消息视图和聊天标签页保持同步，也很难看出你只想递增然后再递减。

cues.en: You want don't to do either of those more than once.
cues.zh: 你不想让这两者中的任何一个执行超过一次。

cues.en: And as we add more features, this code just only gets longer.
cues.zh: 随着我们添加更多功能，这段代码只会越来越长。

cues.en: And having something imperative like this basically led us to the situation where we had our most annoying chat bug happen over and over.
cues.zh: 这种命令式的代码基本上导致我们陷入了最烦人的聊天Bug反复出现的境地。

cues.en: Would get an unseen count, and there would be no unseen messages behind it. Everyone's sort of used to seeing one of these numbers, clicking on it, you get something new behind it.
cues.zh: 会获取到一个未读计数，但背后却没有任何未读消息。大家基本上都习惯了看到这种数字，点击它，然后背后就会有新内容。

cues.en: That's exciting. But when they get that number and they click, there's nothing there. They refresh the page and it's gone. That's really annoying. It's really frustrating.
cues.zh: 这很棒。但当他们拿到这个数字并点击时，却什么也没有。他们刷新页面，数字就消失了。这真的很烦人，非常让人沮丧。

cues.en: And that's what of what led to the whole
cues.zh: 这就是导致整个

cues.en: fixed chat user feedback.
cues.zh: 修复聊天用户反馈的原因。

cues.en: And it wasn't like we didn't fix the problem. We would always fix some particular edge case, but this problem would keep coming back just because the whole system was fragile.
cues.zh: 倒也不是说我们没解决问题。我们总是能修复某些特定的边缘情况，但这个问题总会不断复现，仅仅是因为整个系统太脆弱了。

cues.en: And that was a good sign that something was fundamentally wrong here.
cues.zh: 这是一个好迹象，说明这里有根本性的问题。

cues.en: So how can Flux help with something like this?
cues.zh: 那么Flux如何帮助解决这样的问题呢？

cues.en: If we're looking at the structure of the code that we had before, we have sort of the fundamental pieces. We have chat tab main messages and unseen counter.
cues.zh: 如果我们看看之前代码的结构，我们有基本的组成部分。我们有聊天标签页、主要消息和未读计数器。

cues.en: And then we have an external handler that goes in and changes some of their state. They each have their own state, but the handler goes and modifies them. All of the logic to modify state based on a new message coming in is in the handler itself.
cues.zh: 然后我们有一个外部处理器，它进入并改变它们的一些状态。它们各自有自己的状态，但处理器去修改它们。基于新消息到来修改状态的所有逻辑都在处理器本身中。

cues.en: And so those three different pieces no longer have the ability to maintain internal consistency.
cues.zh: 因此，这三个不同的部分不再有能力维持内部一致性。

cues.en: Basically don't have that information. They've already seeded that control to the handler.
cues.zh: 基本上没有那些信息。它们已经把控制权交给了处理器。

cues.en: What we want to do instead
cues.zh: 我们想要做的相反

cues.en: is internalize this control.
cues.zh: 是将这种控制内化。

cues.en: We want to move all of the control into the individual pieces so that the state is right next to the logic that updates that state.
cues.zh: 我们想把所有控制移到各个部分中，这样状态就紧挨着更新该状态的逻辑。

cues.en: So for chat tab and main messages, it's pretty easy. You just want to append a message whenever you get a new message.
cues.zh: 所以对于聊天标签页和主要消息，这很简单。你只需在收到新消息时追加一条消息。

cues.en: But it's a little bit less clear what to do with the unseen counter. We know that you want to still increment whenever you get a new message, but where do you decrement that unseen counter?
cues.zh: 但对于未读计数器来说，该怎么做就不太清楚了。我们知道你仍然想在收到新消息时递增，但你在哪里递减那个未读计数器呢？

cues.en: You don't have enough information at that point.
cues.zh: 在那个时候你没有足够的信息。

cues.en: What this structure makes clear is that we need more explicit data.
cues.zh: 这种结构清楚地表明我们需要更明确的数据。

cues.en: What we really want is to keep track of a list of the unseen threads, not just the unseen count.
cues.zh: 我们真正想做的是跟踪未读线程列表，而不只是未读数量。

cues.en: And then what we can do is whenever a new message comes in, we can add that thread to the list. And then further down the line, we can have the UI decide when to mark that message as or that thread as seen, and I can remove it from
cues.zh: 这样一来，每当有新消息到达，我们就可以把对应线程添加到列表中。之后，我们可以让 UI 决定何时将这条消息或这个线程标记为已读，然后我就可以把它从

cues.en: information this way means that that thread list stays more consistent. If we put in two Mark seen messages,
cues.zh: 列表中移除。这样能让线程列表保持更一致。如果我们发出两次标记已读的消息，

cues.en: no harm done. The second one is a no op because that thread has already been removed.
cues.zh: 也没有关系。第二次操作不会产生任何效果，因为该线程已经被移除了。

cues.en: So what we learned here is that we should use more explicit data on the client instead of derived data. In this case, what that means is the unseen threads list
cues.zh: 所以我们从中了解到，客户端应该使用更明确的数据，而不是派生数据。在这个例子中，也就是说，未读线程列表

cues.en: is the explicit data,
cues.zh: 就是明确数据，

cues.en: and the unseen count is the derived data, which is the length of that list.
cues.zh: 而未读数量是派生数据，也就是该列表的长度。

cues.en: And doing it this way gives the client a lot more control and a better ability to stay consistent overall.
cues.zh: 这样做可以让客户端拥有更多控制权，也能更好地保持整体一致性。

cues.en: We also knew that we wanted to separate data from our view state. This isn't too different from MEC.
cues.zh: 我们也知道，需要将数据与视图状态分离。这和 MVC 并没有太大区别。

cues.en: You know, it's very
cues.zh: 你知道，这非常

cues.en: non controversial.
cues.zh: 没有争议。

cues.en: But it does add to our system
cues.zh: 但它确实让我们的系统

cues.en: diagram a little bit. So now we have an action coming in to the messages threads and unseen threads state.
cues.zh: 图变得稍微复杂了一点。现在，我们有一个 action 进入消息线程状态和未读线程状态。

cues.en: And whenever those update, they tell the views, hey, something changed and you should go rerender.
cues.zh: 每当这些状态更新时，它们就会通知视图：“有变化了，你应该重新渲染。”

cues.en: The biggest difference
cues.zh: 最大的区别

cues.en: between flux and MVC is that we want to avoid cascading effects by preventing nested updates.
cues.zh: 在 Flux 和 MVC 之间，是我们希望通过阻止嵌套更新来避免级联影响。

cues.en: So what does that mean? Well, if we look at our system,
cues.zh: 所以这意味着什么呢？嗯，如果我们看一下我们的系统，

cues.en: what that means is that we want to let the data layer completely finish processing before we trigger any additional actions.
cues.zh: 这意味着我们希望让数据层完全处理完毕，然后再触发任何额外的操作。

cues.en: In this case, it means that the actions come in, messages, threads, and unseen threads stores
cues.zh: 在这种情况下，这意味着当操作、消息、线程以及未读线程存储进来时，

cues.en: finish processing that, tell the views to update, and only then can the views say, I want to mark something as seen, and that goes back in through the system.
cues.zh: 完成对这些的处理，通知视图进行更新，直到这时视图才能说，我想把某个东西标记为已读，然后这会再次通过系统流转回去。

cues.en: The benefit here is that there are no arrows going in the other direction.
cues.zh: 这样做的好处是，没有反方向流动的箭头。

cues.en: More generally,
cues.zh: 更一般地说，

cues.en: what this diagram looks like is you have an action that comes into the stores, stores update the views,
cues.zh: 这个图表看起来就像是：有一个操作进入存储（stores），存储更新视图（views），

cues.en: and all of your actions take the same structure. Nothing goes in the other direction.
cues.zh: 并且你所有的操作都采用相同的结构。没有任何东西向相反方向流动。

cues.en: And having all of your actions go through the same flow makes it really easy to onboard a new person. When I was working on the teams that used the system,
cues.zh: 让所有的操作都走同一个流程，能让新员工极快地上手。当我在使用这个系统的团队工作时，

cues.en: intuitively,
cues.zh: 直觉上，

cues.en: I wanted to go and basically sit down with a new person and try to wrap them up quickly, tell them sort of everything they needed to know.
cues.zh: 我本想坐下来带带新人，让他们快速上手，把他们需要知道的事情大致都讲一遍。

cues.en: But what we found is that this wasn't really needed with a system like this, because what they could do is trace how one action flowed through the entire system and have a pretty good idea of how the rest of the system worked.
cues.zh: 但我们发现，对于这样一个系统，这其实并不是必需的，因为他们可以通过追踪一个操作是如何流经整个系统的，来对其余系统的工作原理有一个相当不错的了解。

cues.en: And that is what really helped us move more quickly.
cues.zh: 而这正是真正帮助我们提升行动速度的原因。

cues.en: So going back to our original diagram for Flux,
cues.zh: 所以回到我们最初的 Flux 图表，

cues.en: we still have the action, the store, and the view. We also have a dispatcher in here that's the traffic controller of the whole system. What it does is it ensures that until your store layer is completely done, the views or anything else can't put an action through the system.
cues.zh: 我们仍然有 action、store 和 view。这里我们还有一个 dispatcher，它是整个系统的流量控制中心。它的作用是确保在你的 store 层完全完成之前，view 或任何其他东西都无法将 action 传入系统。

cues.en: Instead, if it gets an action while the data layer is still processing, it can throw.
cues.zh: 反之，如果数据层还在处理时它收到了一个操作，它就可以抛出异常。

cues.en: And it just... It's a good constraint to have. It does seem constraining, but that's
cues.zh: 而且它就……这是个很好的约束。看起来确实很受限，但那是

cues.en: a... That's... That constraint is a guarantee for all future developers, including yourself.
cues.zh: 一个……那是……这个约束是对所有未来开发者的保证，包括你自己。

cues.en: It's a guarantee that if you understand where your action starts and what it changes inside of the data layer,
cues.zh: 它保证了只要你清楚操作从哪开始、在数据层里改了什么，

cues.en: you know all of the downstream effects. It doesn't have anything that, you know,
cues.zh: 你就知道所有下游的影响。它不会有什么，你知道，

cues.en: propagates and cascades on down that that crazy graph with all the arrows.
cues.zh: 沿着那张满是箭头的疯狂图表一路传播和级联下去的东西。

cues.en: It's single directional. It goes in one direction.
cues.zh: 它是单向的。只朝一个方向走。

cues.en: And once you finish the single layer, you're done.
cues.zh: 一旦你处理完这一层，就结束了。

cues.en: If we imagine this flux diagram with more stores and more views,
cues.zh: 如果我们想象这个 Flux 图有更多的 store 和更多的 view，

cues.en: it all collapses down to the same thing because all of the arrows go in the same direction.
cues.zh: 它最终都会收敛成同样的东西，因为所有箭头都朝同一个方向。

cues.en: With MVC, you can't form
cues.zh: 用 MVC，你没法形成

cues.en: a simple mental model because the arrows go in both directions.
cues.zh: 一个简单的心智模型，因为箭头是双向的。

cues.en: But with
cues.zh: 但用

cues.en: the arrows going in a single direction, you can collapse it down to exactly this diagram, and that's your mental model for the whole thing.
cues.zh: 单向的箭头，你就能把它收敛成完全就是这张图，这就是你对整件事的心智模型。

cues.en: Alright. So when we switched over to Flux,
cues.zh: 好。所以当我们切换到 Flux 时，

cues.en: in our chat system,
cues.zh: 在我们的聊天系统里，

cues.en: found we is that it improved our data consistency.
cues.zh: 发现它提升了我们的数据一致性。

cues.en: So that if you look at your chat tab and your messages view, they would always be in sync.
cues.zh: 这样如果你看聊天标签页和消息视图，它们始终是同步的。

cues.en: It became a lot easier to pinpoint the root of a bug. So when other employees came to us with bug reports and they described what happened to them, we would usually be able to say, hey, I think it's that module. That's the most likely suspect.
cues.zh: 定位 bug 的根源变得容易多了。所以当其他同事带着 bug 报告来找我们、描述他们遇到的情况时，我们通常都能说，嘿，我觉得是那个模块。那是最可能的嫌疑对象。

cues.en: And that actually helped us move really quickly because instead of trying to trace through a handler and all the downstream effects there, we could just say, it's probably this module. Let me go look at it. And that shortened our iteration cycle.
cues.zh: 这确实帮我们加快了速度，因为不用再去追查一个处理器以及它带来的各种下游影响，我们只需要说，问题多半出在这个模块，去看一眼就行。这就缩短了我们的迭代周期。

cues.en: And finally, we were able to write more meaningful unit tests as a result of this. What does that mean? Well, because all of the state and all of the logic that updates the state is in the same place,
cues.zh: 最后，我们也因此能写出更有意义的单元测试。这是什么意思呢？因为所有状态、以及所有更新状态的逻辑都放在同一个地方，

cues.en: we basically could test that module by saying, let's assume that you're in state A, give it an input,
cues.zh: 我们基本上可以这样测试那个模块：假设你处在状态 A，给它一个输入，

cues.en: and now we can test that it's in the expected state B, and that state B is consistent.
cues.zh: 然后就能验证它是否处于预期的状态 B，以及这个状态 B 是否一致。

cues.en: A lot of our unit tests looked like this, and they were really effective and helped us avoid making the same mistake twice.
cues.zh: 我们的很多单元测试都是这么写的，效果非常好，帮我们避免了重复踩同一个坑。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So we've looked at a lot of boxes. We've made a lot of abstract arguments.
cues.zh: 我们看了很多方框图，也讲了很多抽象的道理。

cues.en: What was the real world impact of this?
cues.zh: 那它到底带来了什么实际影响呢？

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: our most common chat bug, that zombie unseen count that would go away as soon as you clicked on it, we stopped seeing that,
cues.zh: 我们最常见的聊天 bug，就是那个“僵尸未读数”，一点开就消失的那个，再也没有出现过，

cues.en: finally.
cues.zh: 总算没了。

cues.en: And we stopped annoying our users every time they tried to chat, saw a drastic drop
cues.zh: 用户每次想聊天时也不会再被烦到，关于聊天的

cues.en: tickets about chat.
cues.zh: 工单数量大幅下降。

cues.en: And most importantly,
cues.zh: 最重要的是，

cues.en: this bug hasn't been back to haunt us. Like I said before, we would always fix it. But every time we add features and every time we change logic behind it, this bug used to come back. Once we change the underlying system, the underlying architecture,
cues.zh: 这个 bug 再也没回来纠缠过我们。就像我之前说的，我们每次都能修好它，但每次加新功能、每次改动它背后的逻辑，这个 bug 都会卷土重来。而一旦我们改掉了底层的系统和架构，

cues.en: this bug went away for good.
cues.zh: 这个 bug 就彻底消失了。

cues.en: Alright. So at this point, we're in a pretty good state with our data flow.
cues.zh: 好了，到这里我们的数据流已经相当不错了。

cues.en: But our rendering layer was still a little bit difficult.
cues.zh: 但我们的渲染层还是有点难搞。

cues.en: The initial render is pretty easy. I have a list of messages come in from the data layer. That renders into the markup for the list of messages.
cues.zh: 初次渲染很简单。我从数据层拿到一系列消息，再渲染成消息列表的标记。

cues.en: Still pretty manageable. But whenever we wanted to update it, we didn't want to just rerender the entire thing.
cues.zh: 还是比较好处理的。但每次想要更新它时，我们并不想直接重新渲染整个内容。

cues.en: We wanted to optimize it a little bit for the new message case,
cues.zh: 我们想针对新消息这种情况稍作优化，

cues.en: because that happens so frequently,
cues.zh: 因为这种情况太常见了，

cues.en: and you might have a really long list of messages. And users might notice, you know, if we start rerendering every time and the UI flickers.
cues.zh: 你可能会有很长的消息列表。如果每次重新渲染导致界面闪烁，用户就会注意到。

cues.en: So what we had instead is the rendering layer would look at the messages list
cues.zh: 因此，我们实际采用的方式是，渲染层会查看消息列表。

cues.en: that the data layer gave
cues.zh: 数据层提供的

cues.en: it and find that it has one more message than previously,
cues.zh: 并发现它比之前多了一条消息，

cues.en: and it would translate that into an append operation.
cues.zh: 然后把它转换成追加操作。

cues.en: The problem with this code is that it became really fragile over time. We had to account for different message types. We had to account for messages coming in out of order.
cues.zh: 这段代码的问题在于，随着时间推移，它变得非常脆弱。我们不得不考虑不同的消息类型，还得考虑消息乱序到达的情况。

cues.en: And this code just got more fragile over time.
cues.zh: 而这段代码随时间推移变得越来越脆弱。

cues.en: We had we had one guy on the team who knew it, like Tom said,
cues.zh: 我们团队里曾有一个人懂这个，就像Tom说的，

cues.en: and nobody else on the team wanted to touch it. Everyone else was willing to to jump in on any other bug in the data layer because they were comfortable with it. But intuitively, they knew that this code was fragile,
cues.zh: 团队里没人愿意碰它。其他人愿意接手数据层的任何其他 bug，因为那些他们熟悉。但凭直觉，他们知道这段代码很脆弱，

cues.en: that it was too difficult to change without breaking something else, and they just wanted to refer to the one guy on the team who understood everything.
cues.zh: 说改动它太难，难免会弄坏别的东西，他们只想找团队里那个什么都懂的人。

cues.en: So that's kind of a bad sign.
cues.zh: 这可不是什么好兆头。

cues.en: What we really wanted for our rendering system was to be able to always rerender, no matter what.
cues.zh: 对于我们渲染系统，真正想要的是无论什么情况都能始终重新渲染。

cues.en: Give it a list of messages, we know how to render that
cues.zh: 给它一个消息列表，我们知道如何渲染它

cues.en: list into the DOM.
cues.zh: 把列表放入 DOM。

cues.en: What we really wanted was a rendering library that would efficiently do that change for us without interrupting the user experience.
cues.zh: 我们真正想要的，是一个能高效完成这种变更、又不打断用户体验的渲染库。

cues.en: This is where React comes in, and here's Pete to talk about how React solves this problem.
cues.zh: 这就轮到 React 登场了，下面请 Pete 来讲讲 React 是如何解决这个问题的。

cues.en: Hey everybody.
cues.zh: 大家好。

cues.en: I'm Pete and I work on the React team here at Facebook and I also manage the Instagram web team.
cues.zh: 我是Pete，在Facebook的React团队工作，同时也负责管理Instagram web团队。

cues.en: Flux gets your data model into a really predictable state. It's very easy for you to understand what's going to happen in your system.
cues.zh: Flux 让你的数据模型进入非常可预测的状态。你很容易理解系统里接下来会发生什么。

cues.en: But Jing brought up a really important point which is we have to render this consistent data model to the user interface and that's a pretty difficult problem.
cues.zh: 但Jing提出了一个非常重要的点，就是我们得把这个一致的数据模型渲染到用户界面上，而这是个相当棘手的问题。

cues.en: So difficult in fact that we built a user interface library called React designed to solve the hardest problem in this space,
cues.zh: 事实上，这太难了，所以我们构建了一个名为 React 的用户界面库，旨在解决这个领域中最难的问题，

cues.en: which is that data changing over time is the root of all evil.
cues.zh: 也就是说，数据随时间变化是万恶之源。

cues.en: So here's an example piece of user interface
cues.zh: 下面是一个用户界面的示例

cues.en: from our chat product. It's the buddy list.
cues.zh: 来自我们的聊天产品。是好友列表。

cues.en: Now I'm going to read off a series of mutations to this buddy list and I'm going to ask you what the state of this should be at the end. So I'm going to ask you what it should look like. Are guys have this memorized?
cues.zh: 现在我要读出一系列对这个好友列表的修改操作，然后问你这个列表最后应该是什么状态。我会问你它应该是什么样子。你们都记住了吗？

cues.en: Alright. I know it's after lunch, but I'm gonna assume you guys memorized it. Alright. Let's go. Ready?
cues.zh: 好，我知道午饭刚过，但我假设你们都记住了，好，开始吧，准备好了吗？

cues.en: So Alice went offline,
cues.zh: Alice 下线了，

cues.en: Bob went offline, Steve went online, Bob went online,
cues.zh: Bob 下线了，Steve 上线了，Bob 上线了，

cues.en: Charles is idle, and Charles is on mobile. What
cues.zh: Charles 空闲，而且 Charles 用的是手机。那么

cues.en: does this user interface look like? Does anybody know?
cues.zh: 这个用户界面长什么样？有人知道吗？

cues.en: I don't know. Have no idea. Because processes that are spread out over time are very difficult for humans to understand and hold in their head. Just these imperative actions that mutate state. It's very difficult for you to figure out what that state is at the end of that sequence of mutations.
cues.zh: 我不知道，完全没头绪。因为随时间展开的进程对人类来说太难理解和记住了，就是这些不断改变状态的命令式操作。你很难搞清楚在一连串变更之后，最终状态到底是什么。

cues.en: And I'm not the first person to discover this. Dijkstra
cues.zh: 我不是第一个发现这个问题的人。Dijkstra

cues.en: has a really great quote about this. He says, We should do our utmost to shorten the conceptual gap between the static program and the dynamic process
cues.zh: 对此有句很精辟的话。他说，我们应当竭尽全力缩短静态程序与动态进程之间的概念鸿沟，

cues.en: so that to make the correspondence between the program and the process as trivial as possible.
cues.zh: 让程序与进程之间的对应关系尽可能简单明了。

cues.en: Now what Dijkstra is saying here is he's saying we need to take this series of imperative mutations,
cues.zh: Dijkstra 这里的意思是，我们需要把这串命令式变更，

cues.en: these things that are changing over time and try to make it look like a program that executes at a single point in time. So if you go back to that buddy list example I was just talking about,
cues.zh: 这些随时间变化的东西，设法让它看起来像是一个在单一时间点执行的程序。所以回到我刚才说的好友列表例子，

cues.en: if I present a consistent snapshot of the data at any point in time, it's very easy for you to visualize what this user interface should actually look like. You can imagine how we would draw this on the screen.
cues.zh: 如果我在任意时间点呈现出一致的数据快照，你就很容易想象出这个用户界面实际该长什么样。你能想象我们该怎么把它画到屏幕上。

cues.en: Back in the ninety's when we were doing server rendered apps all the time, we didn't have a lot of JavaScript running on the client. This is actually how we wrote user interfaces.
cues.zh: 九十年代我们一直做服务端渲染应用时，客户端上运行的 JavaScript 并不多。这实际上就是我们当时编写用户界面的方式。

cues.en: When the data changed in your application,
cues.zh: 当应用中的数据发生变化时，

cues.en: you simply hit the refresh button in your browser. And what would happen is the browser would go to the server,
cues.zh: 你只需在浏览器里点一下刷新按钮。接下来会发生什么？浏览器会去服务器，

cues.en: fetch some data from the database which would be a consistent snapshot of the state of your application.
cues.zh: 从数据库拉取数据，那会是应用状态的一致快照。

cues.en: It would turn it into an HTML page and flush it down to the browser.
cues.zh: 服务器把它转成 HTML 页面，再刷给浏览器。

cues.en: So what we've done with React is we've taken the mental model of a
cues.zh: 所以在 React 里我们做的事，就是把

cues.en: server rendered web app and we've brought it to the client.
cues.zh: 服务端渲染 Web 应用的心智模型搬到了客户端。

cues.en: So whenever the data changes, whether it's from Flux
cues.zh: 于是每当数据变化，不管来自 Flux

cues.en: or Parse
cues.zh: 还是 Parse

cues.en: or Firebase or Backbone or whatever you're using to get data on the client, React
cues.zh: 还是 Firebase、Backbone，或者你在客户端取数据用的任何东西，React

cues.en: conceptually re render the entire component every single time just like a nineties era web app.
cues.zh: 在概念上每次都会重新渲染整个组件，就像九十年代的 Web 应用一样。

cues.en: Now when I say nineties era web app, what really mean is a RESTful web service.
cues.zh: 我说九十年代的 Web 应用，真正指的是 RESTful Web 服务。

cues.en: So if you're bringing that model to the client, you get a lot of the benefits of RESTful architecture for free. So one of the important parts of RESTful architectures is item potency and a similar concept is referential transparency.
cues.zh: 把这个模型搬到客户端，你就能免费获得 RESTful 架构的许多好处。RESTful 架构的重要部分之一就是幂等性，类似的概念是引用透明性。

cues.en: When
cues.zh: 当

cues.en: you model your UI as a referentially transparent function,
cues.zh: 你把 UI 建模成引用透明的函数时，

cues.en: you get a lot of benefits. Think about how the web works today.
cues.zh: 你会得到很多好处。想想今天的 Web 是怎么运作的。

cues.en: When you type a URL in, you always get the same resource no matter what.
cues.zh: 当你在地址栏输入一个 URL，无论怎样，你得到的总是同一个资源。

cues.en: With React,
cues.zh: 用 React 时，

cues.en: when you put in data, you always get the same user interface rendered at any point in time.
cues.zh: 你输入数据，在任何时间点渲染出来的用户界面总是相同的。

cues.en: Whenever the data changes, you can simply re fetch and refresh just like in the nineties.
cues.zh: 只要数据变了，你直接重新获取、刷新就行，就像九十年代那样。

cues.en: One of the reasons why people use RESTful architecture so much is because they're so predictable. It's very easy to cache them. You understand the performance characteristics and how to scale them out simply because for the same set of inputs, you get the same set of outputs.
cues.zh: 人们如此爱用 RESTful 架构，原因之一就是它非常可预测。缓存起来很容易。你能清楚它的性能特性，也懂得如何横向扩展，就是因为同一组输入永远得到同一组输出。

cues.en: And a lot of great stuff falls out of this like testability.
cues.zh: 由此还能顺带得到很多好处，比如可测试性。

cues.en: A lot of our unit tests for our user interfaces at Facebook started out as
cues.zh: 我们在 Facebook 为界面写的很多单元测试，最初都是这样的：

cues.en: click on this button, mutate this state, a series of imperative actions and then we would make some assertions along the way.
cues.zh: 点这个按钮、改这个状态，一系列命令式操作，然后沿途做一些断言。

cues.en: Since we've adopted this model,
cues.zh: 自从采用这个模型之后，

cues.en: we do lot less of that and a lot more of sending in a consistent state and making some assertions on what was actually rendered based on that state.
cues.zh: 这类测试我们写得少多了，更多是传入一个确定的状态，然后针对基于该状态实际渲染出的结果做断言。

cues.en: Now this sounds like a pretty great model for building applications but we can't do this with the regular browser APIs we have today.
cues.zh: 这听起来是个很棒的构建应用的模型，但用我们今天现有的常规浏览器 API 做不到。

cues.en: And the reason for that is that the DOM is stateful.
cues.zh: 原因在于 DOM 是有状态的。

cues.en: So if we were to re render all of the DOM nodes whenever anything changed in our application,
cues.zh: 所以，如果应用里任何东西一变，我们就把所有 DOM 节点重新渲染一遍，

cues.en: we would have a really poor performance profile and really bad user experience.
cues.zh: 性能会非常差，用户体验也会非常糟。

cues.en: The browser was not designed to be constantly creating and throwing out DOM nodes. And additionally, if somebody's typing into a text field or has an inertial scroll going on, if we were to throw out those DOM nodes and recreate them,
cues.zh: 浏览器最初并不是为了不断创建和丢弃 DOM 节点而设计的。而且，如果有人在文本框中输入，或者正在进行惯性滚动，要是我们丢掉那些 DOM 节点再重新创建，

cues.en: we would kill that scroll momentum and scroll position and it would just be a really bad user experience.
cues.zh: 就会破坏滚动的惯性和位置，用户体验会非常糟糕。

cues.en: And this actually isn't limited to the browser. This is any stateful UI toolkit. So imagine implementing this on iOS and UI kit. People generally don't destroy and recreate view hierarchies on every change because of the performance characteristics and because of the user experience problems.
cues.zh: 这其实不限于浏览器。任何有状态的 UI 工具包都是如此。想象一下在 iOS 和 UIKit 上实现这个。人们通常不会在每次变更时销毁并重建视图层级，因为性能特性，也因为用户体验问题。

cues.en: So what we did at Facebook is we spent the past couple of years building what we like to call a virtual DOM abstraction
cues.zh: 所以我们在 Facebook 做的事是，过去几年里构建了我们喜欢称之为虚拟 DOM 抽象的东西

cues.en: which is implemented in this library called React.
cues.zh: 它实现在一个叫 React 的库中。

cues.en: And what the virtual DOM lets us do is it lets us model our UI in the way that I just described, conceptually re rendering everything
cues.zh: 虚拟 DOM 让我们能做的，就是按我刚才描述的方式为 UI 建模，在概念上重新渲染所有内容

cues.en: in an inexpensive and good way for user experience.
cues.zh: 以一种低成本且对用户体验友好的方式。

cues.en: So here's how it works.
cues.zh: 下面是它的工作原理。

cues.en: Whenever the data changes, we rerender your application to the virtual DOM and we create a new tree of virtual DOM nodes.
cues.zh: 每当数据变化时，我们把你的应用重新渲染到虚拟 DOM，并创建一棵新的虚拟 DOM 节点树。

cues.en: Then we diff that new tree of virtual DOM nodes with the previous tree, the one that existed before the data changed.
cues.zh: 然后我们把新的虚拟 DOM 节点树与之前的树做 diff，也就是数据变化之前存在的那棵树。

cues.en: Then we can isolate what were the changes between the two virtual DOM trees and we can compute the minimal set of DOM mutations necessary
cues.zh: 接着我们就能找出两棵虚拟 DOM 树之间的差异，并计算出所需的最小 DOM 变更集合

cues.en: to make the real DOM look like the virtual DOM. We put that into a queue and we flush that queue
cues.zh: 让真实 DOM 看起来像虚拟 DOM。我们把它放进一个队列，然后刷新这个队列

cues.en: update the UI.
cues.zh: 更新 UI。

cues.en: Here's an example of how that works.
cues.zh: 这是一个示例，说明它是如何工作的。

cues.en: Remember the buddy list example?
cues.zh: 还记得好友列表那个例子吗？

cues.en: We have the initial state that I showed you in the screenshot on the left and we have the state that we want to get to after all those mutations on the right.
cues.zh: 左边是我在截图里展示的初始状态，右边是经过所有这些变更后我们想要达到的状态。

cues.en: Now again, we can't just throw out the DOM nodes and re render them for the performance and user experience reasons I just mentioned.
cues.zh: 同样，由于我刚才提到的性能和用户体验原因，我们不能直接丢弃 DOM 节点并重新渲染它们。

cues.en: So we have a virtual
cues.zh: 所以我们有一个虚拟

cues.en: DOM diffing algorithm that goes through and highlights what actually changed in these two data structures. So I've colored those changes in yellow.
cues.zh: DOM 差异算法，它会遍历并高亮出这两个数据结构中实际发生变化的部分。我把这些变化标成了黄色。

cues.en: What the system will do is it'll eventually turn it into imperative DOM mutations just like people write on the web today.
cues.zh: 系统最终会把它转换成命令式 DOM 变更，就像如今人们在 Web 上写的那样。

cues.en: Now
cues.zh: 现在

cues.en: remember,
cues.zh: 记住，

cues.en: this is actually the most difficult part of the engineering of the UI. These imperative mutations that change over time. If you think back to that buddy list example,
cues.zh: 这实际上是 UI 工程中最困难的部分。这些随时间变化的命令式变更。如果你回想一下那个好友列表的例子，

cues.en: this is the same thing. This is just the code representation of those mutations.
cues.zh: 这是一回事。这只是那些变更的代码表示。

cues.en: But the the key here is we push the complexity of those mutations
cues.zh: 但关键在于，我们把那些变更的复杂性

cues.en: into the framework
cues.zh: 推给了框架

cues.en: so the end user of the library doesn't even need to think about it. So they think about how their UI looks like at any point in time as a complete snapshot and the system figures out the imperative mutations needed to update the UI to make it look correct.
cues.zh: 所以这个库的最终用户甚至不需要考虑它。他们只需把 UI 在任意时间点的样子想成一个完整的快照，系统会找出更新 UI 所需的命令式变更，让它看起来正确。

cues.en: So
cues.zh: 所以

cues.en: if you've been following so far, this might not seem like a very performance system because we're re rendering our UI all the time to this virtual representation
cues.zh: 如果你一直跟到现在，这可能看起来不像一个性能很好的系统，因为我们一直把 UI 重新渲染到这个虚拟表示

cues.en: and we're diffing a lot of things that may not have actually changed. In this example, only two pieces of data changed out of that whole DOM structure.
cues.zh: 而且我们在对许多可能并未实际改变的东西做差异比较。在这个例子里，整个 DOM 结构中只有两处数据发生了变化。

cues.en: The good news is this is how high performance three d games work. One of my colleagues built a game a couple years ago called Doom three and here's how it works.
cues.zh: 好消息是，高性能3D游戏就是这么运作的。我的一位同事几年前做了一个叫Doom 3的游戏，它是这样工作的。

cues.en: We have the game state that represents the consistent state of the world.
cues.zh: 我们有游戏状态，它表示世界的一致状态。

cues.en: We have user input events that come in and mutate that state and we have network events that come in from the game server.
cues.zh: 我们有用户输入事件进来并改变那个状态，还有来自游戏服务器的网络事件。

cues.en: And that world state goes into the front end of the game. Now the front end of the game represents all the rules of the world. So how players move around, how weapons work,
cues.zh: 那个世界状态进入游戏的前端。游戏的前端表示了世界的所有规则。比如玩家如何移动、武器如何运作，

cues.en: that type of thing.
cues.zh: 诸如此类。

cues.en: And out of that component comes what we like to call a scene intermediate representation, which is a logical declarative description of what needs to actually be drawn.
cues.zh: 从这个组件输出的是我们喜欢称之为场景中间表示的东西，它是对实际需要绘制内容的逻辑声明式描述。

cues.en: Now they take that logical description of what needs to be drawn, they put it into the back end, which turns it into OpenGL operations that are imperative and go over the bus to the graphics card.
